_comment: What the committed @visual baselines DEPICT, as a hash of the render input rather than a date.
Regenerate with `pnpm gen:visual-fingerprints` in the SAME commit as a baseline capture; the
capture job in .github/workflows/e2e-manual.yml does it for you and stamps capturedIn with the
runner's SHA. Never hand-edit a fingerprint to silence test/e2e/template-fingerprints.test.ts:
that says the PNGs show something they do not.
This is a drift DETECTOR with a visible manual override, not an unforgeable proof. A local
regeneration stamps capturedIn 'local', which greens the gate but marks in the file that no
capture stands behind it - and LIVE-040's probe rejects 'local', so only a runner capture closes
that row. capturedIn is provenance for a reader, not an input to the gate: the gate compares
fingerprints only, so it works in the depth-1 clone CI and agents actually get.
NO `home` ENTRY, AND THAT IS THE POINT (HYG-095). Every page here resolves the PUBLISHED
document first and only falls back to its template, so a template fingerprint is meaningful
exactly where no published document shadows the slug. By OWN-043 `/` is shadowed, so hashing
getTemplate("home") measured a branch production never takes - and it stayed green when
LIVE-252 rewrote the published document. The shadowed set is READ from scripts/stored-links.json,
never typed here, so publishing a second page drops it from coverage on its own.
